equivalent.reason: ReleaseState::can_advance_to returns before it calls forward when the two states are equal, and position gives distinct states distinct indices, so forward never compares two equal indices.
Every train label starts with a letter, which sorts after every digit byte, so comparing the label with a numeric first identifier gives Greater, as the arm for a numeric identifier does.
parse_number refuses any identifier that holds a byte other than a digit, so number_against_digits answers Less for a non-numeric second identifier, as the arm for one does.
parse_number only reads identifiers of a valid prerelease, and the semver crate refuses an empty identifier before any prerelease reaches the core, so the digits it reads are never empty.
